Reanchor efficiency research to direct_lifted (0.630432 AUC, 25.02 s inference), using sketch256 (0.620337, 18.15 s) as the observed cost/utility tradeoff; single-seed results remain provisional.

topic.title: Measured cost frontier at the stronger direct_lifted utility level
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can a simpler replacement retain the frozen direct_lifted reference's predictive utility at lower measured training or inference cost, and does it improve the frontier relative to pooled_observed and sketch256?
topic.hypothesis: The substantial utility gap between direct_lifted and sketch256 makes efficiency established against joint_identity insufficient evidence of efficiency at the stronger utility level. A simpler replacement may retain direct_lifted utility, but this transfer is unverified. Retain frozen direct_lifted, pooled_observed and sketch256 as controls; predeclare a utility-retention margin and compare AUC, logloss, parameter counts and repeated training/inference timings under identical measurement conditions. Use matched-capacity replacement controls to distinguish representation effects from capacity, and distinguish information-changing replacements from execution-only changes. Failure to retain utility within the margin, or absence of a reproducible cost reduction, falsifies the proposed efficiency benefit. Single-seed utility differences and timing noise remain alternative explanations; neither source scores nor execution-only equivalence establish a representation mechanism. Reserve resources for attribution and final assessment before expanding the search.
